questions.q:
Which two numbers from amongst the given options should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

168 ÷ 4 + 216 ÷ ( 78 × 1 - 8) = 14
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is:

Find which two number from the among the given options should be interchanged to make the given equation correct.

Let's check each option one by one:

Option 1) 78 and 216

Given: 168 ÷ 4 + 216 ÷ ( 78 × 1 - 8) = 14

After interchanging the numbers we get the;

⇒ 168 ÷ 4 + 78 ÷ ( 216 × 1 - 8) = 14

⇒ 168 ÷ 4 + 78 ÷ 208 = 14

⇒ 42 + 0.375 = 14

⇒ 42.375 ≠ 14

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 2) 14 and 8

Given: 168 ÷ 4 + 216 ÷ ( 78 × 1 - 8) = 14

After interchanging the numbers we get the;

⇒ 168 ÷ 4 + 216 ÷ ( 78 × 1 - 14) = 8

⇒ 168 ÷ 4 + 216 ÷ 64 = 8

⇒ 42 + 3.375 = 8

⇒ 45.375 ≠ 8

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 3) 78 and 14

Given: 168 ÷ 4 + 216 ÷ ( 78 × 1 - 8) = 14

After interchanging the numbers we get the;

⇒ 168 ÷ 4 + 216 ÷ (14 × 1 - 8) = 78

⇒ 168 ÷ 4 + 216 ÷ 6 = 78

⇒ 42 + 36 = 78

⇒ 78 = 78

⇒ LHS = RHS

Option 4) 216 and 168

Given: 168 ÷ 4 + 216 ÷ ( 78 × 1 - 8) = 14

After interchanging the numbers we get the;

⇒ 216 ÷ 4 + 168 ÷ ( 78 × 1 - 8) = 14

⇒ 216 ÷ 4 + 168 ÷ 70 = 14

⇒ 54 + 2.4 = 14

⇒ 56.4 ≠ 14

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".

questions.q: Based on Macaulay’s Minute, the English Education Act was introduced in .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1835.

Key Points

• In 1834 Thomas Babington Macaulay came to India as a Legal Member of the Council of India.

• He formulated his policy proposal in his Minute on Indian Education, delivered in Kolkata on 2nd February 1835.

• As per Lord Macaulay’s “Minutes on Indian Education” ‘Literature’ meant English literature and not Sanskrit or Arabic or Persian literature.

• He emphasized that the medium of instruction should be English.

• His thinking was to change Indian culture.

• The Governor-General of India, William Bentinck, approved the proposal of Lord Macaulay on 7th March 1835.

• It became the cornerstone of British-Indian educational policy until Independence (and remained largely in force after that as well)

Additional InformationHunter Commisssion

• The Hunter Commission has an important place in the field of education in India.

• At the primary level, the commission emphasized on teaching useful subjects in the local language.

• Lord Ripon set up a commission under the chairmanship of Sir William Hunter in 1882 AD, whose task was to consider the irrelevance of the Woods Dispatch of 1854.

Woods Dispatch

• The education system of present India is the gift of Charles Wood.

• The East India company policy to change renews the charter after every 20 years, so that time in 1853.

• The parliament board surveyed Indian Education System and determined that there was a huge need for education.

• Wood was the President and he sent the report to East India Company the report was forwarded as a dispatch to the Indian Government on 19th July 1854 and this is known as Wood’s Dispatch 1854.

• The Wood’s Dispatch is considered the Magna Carta of English education in India.

• Despatch expressed that education in English, as well as Indian local languages, should be enhanced and encouraged throughout the Nation.

• They wanted to establish a Department of Public Instruction in every province.
